newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa product exports rose in June.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa product exports rose in June.

text.p: Ivory Coast's semi-finished cocoa product and powder exports rose to 8,077 tonnes in June from 5,868 in May, official shipping data show.

Cumulative exports in the first nine months of the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) season -- including shipments from October 1 to October 24, when the season officially opened -- were 69,291 tonnes against 49,161 in 1995/96.
Cocoa liquor, butter and paste shipments from Abidjan totalled 5,440 tonnes. Another 2,161 tonnes left from San Pedro.
The data do not separate liquor, butter and cake exports but they show shipments of powder from Abidjan totalled 476 tonnes.
Cumulative powder shipments stand at 5,116 tonnes this season against 3,903 tonnes the year before and 63 tonnes in 1994/95 -- before most processing capacity came on line.
Exporters said local factories had taken 1996/97 deliveries totalling over 130,000 tonnes of beans by late July.
Ivory Coast's cocoa bean processing capacity of just over 160,000 tonnes is set to rise in 1997/98 as the government encourages investors to build processing plants to add export value.

Industry analysts expect processors to take over 200,000 tonnes of beans in 1997/98 as more capacity comes on line. Beans can lose up to 20 percent of their raw weight during processing. --Matthew Bunce, Abidjan newsroom + 225 21 90 90
